title: Of the Vedas, the one that is sung
hookLine: a book of songs, Indra, the mind, awareness: one line of the Gita holds them together
carry: vibhuti: god shines through the best of each thing
tomorrow: a hymn for a broken bone

cards: A book of songs. Indra, among the gods. The mind.
Awareness. They share a single line of the Bhagavad Gita. This path has been in that chapter before, the tenth, where Krishna said, among meters, I am the Gayatri.

Earlier in the same list, he names something this week has been listening to. After days of chants, breath and stobhas, it may not be a surprise what. Today, the last day on the Sama Veda: what Krishna says about it.

teach.h: OF THE VEDAS, I AM THE SAMA VEDA.
teach.b: Arjuna has asked how he should think of Krishna, and Krishna answers with a list: in each kind of thing, one where he can be found. Among lights, the sun.
Today's verse, Gita ten, twenty-two, begins: vedanam samavedo 'smi. Of the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda.
Then, in the same breath: among the gods, I am Indra. Among the senses, the mind. In living beings, awareness.
The Gita doesn't stop to explain why the Sama Veda; it says it and moves on. Some readers point to what we've seen these days.

teach.h: THE WORDS, SUNG, BEGIN TO RING.
teach.b: The Sama Veda is the Rig Veda's verses, sung: the words are the same, and what's added is melody. Remember the Chandogya's chain, where the essence of the verse is the chant.
A verse sung is still the verse, but now it rings. Then Krishna gives the key to the whole list.

teach.h: WHATEVER SHINES: A SPARK OF HIS SPLENDOR.
teach.b: In paraphrase: whatever is glorious, beautiful or mighty, know that it springs from a spark of my splendor. These are his vibhutis, the ways his glory shows through the world.
That's a real Hindu way of seeing: God is behind everything, and shows most plainly where something shines.
It's why a family may hear a fine singer's voice as Saraswati's gift, and why a well-sung chant can bring a grandmother to tears. Where should I look for you, Arjuna asked.
One answer from this chapter: in whatever shines, and among the Vedas, in the one that is sung.

how: In the Gita's tenth chapter Krishna names where he can be found, including 'of the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda', and the Sama Veda itself is kept by chanters who learn it by ear.

games.q: what does “the sama veda as song” mean?
o: the Veda Krishna calls the oldest of the four
the Veda Krishna names as himself among the Vedas
the Veda Arjuna is told to set aside for war

s: the Gita explains at length why Krishna names the Sama Veda
it doesn't say why. it names the Sama Veda and moves on, and readers have wondered since.
in the same verse, Krishna says among the gods he is Indra
Sama Veda, Indra, the mind and awareness share one line.
Arjuna's question is where he should think of Krishna
Krishna answers with a list: in each kind of thing, one where he can be found.

games.q: a few verses after naming the Sama Veda, Krishna sums up his whole list for Arjuna. what does he say?
o: look for me only at the fire altar
whatever is glorious springs from a spark of my splendor
look for me only in the Vedas
games.why: these are his vibhutis: wherever something shines, his glory shows. among the Vedas, the one that is sung.

practice: Close or soften your eyes and listen outward, traffic, a fan, a bird, a voice somewhere, the hum of a fridge, without naming anything.
Then ask Arjuna's question gently, where should I look, and let your attention rest on whichever sound feels most like singing, or on your own breath if none does. If you pray, rest in prayer there.

wordCard.voice: The Sama Veda as song. In the Gita, Krishna says: of the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda, the Veda that is sung, one of his vibhutis. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit, Bhagavad Gita 10.22: of the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda.

carryVoice: Your line: vibhuti, God shining through the best of each thing. Among the Vedas, the one that is sung. The songbook, closed for now.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 10.17–22 (Arjuna asks where to think of Krishna; among lights the sun, among mountains Meru; of the Vedas the Sama Veda, among gods Indra, among senses the mind, in beings awareness)
Chandogya Upanishad 1.1.2 (the chant as the essence of the verse)
Bhagavad Gita 10.41 (whatever is glorious, beautiful or mighty springs from a spark of my splendor)
